messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU-serving latency spike on /v1/generate affecting hosted-api. Pg severity P2. start_ts=2026-08-02T15:07:14Z
Alex: Acknowledged. I'm on it – looking at metrics now.
Maria: I see 95th pct token latency ~2.2s up from 0.6s, errors are mostly upstream timeouts. Is this region-specific? :thinking: 
Alex: Seems to be us-east-1 only. Top error is backend timeout to dedicated-gpu-pool-3.
Sam T.: I've put a temp scaling rule to +2 nodes on that pool, can monitor.
Alex: Nice. Also enabling fallback routing to model-quantized-v1 for non-sensitive users.
Jon P.: Customer impact: three paying customers reported increased request times and 500s. Not widespread but high severity for a few tenants. Logged incidents to CS.
Product Ops Bot: Notified owners for customers: acme-corp, finlytics.
Maria: Mitigation looks to reduce latency already down to 0.9s post-scale. Errors dropping.
Alex: Can someone start a short debrief and capture immediate action items? I'll keep running mitigation for another 20m then handoff.
Lee (SRE): I'll take over after you. Can you dump the allocation logs and the pool health?
Alex: Pasted logs to thread (trimmed). ```
[2026-08-02T15:06:55Z] pool=d-gpu-3 scale_fail=0 alloc=95% backlog=42
[2026-08-02T15:07:10Z] route=hosted-api timeout= upstream=dedicated-gpu-pool-3 err=502
``` 
Maria: My quick root-cause hypothesis: autoscaler mis-evaluated incoming long-tail seqs and didn't pick correct burst policy; KV cache thrash causing high GPU memory while kernel switching increased latency.
Sam T.: Agreed. Suggested runbook changes: add explicit check of autoscale burst thresholds and GPU mem pressure before invoking model swaps.
Alex: Let's capture remediation owners and due dates.
Maria: Action items:
- Runbook: add autoscale troubleshooting checklist, owner = Maria, due = 2026-08-09
- Infra: audit autoscale rules for d-gpu pools + add safety cap, owner = Lee, due = 2026-08-05
- Product/CS: notify impacted customers with summary + ETA, owner = Jon P., due = 2026-08-03
- Observability: add a dashboard alert for KV-cache eviction spikes, owner = Sam T., due = 2026-08-06
Alex: I'll create the tracker issue and link the runbook PR template. link: https://redwood.internal/infra/issue/4938
Sam T.: For runbook snippet, propose adding command to check pool status: 
```bash
# check pool utilization
rwdctl pool describe d-gpu-3 --region us-east-1
rwdctl pool metrics d-gpu-3 --since 30m --fields alloc,backlog,mem_usage
```
Jon P.: Scheduling: we should have a 30m tactical debrief tomorrow to finalize post-incident notes and confirm owner progress. Who's in?
Alex: I'm in. 2026-08-03 10:00 US/Eastern works.
Maria: Me.
Lee (SRE): Me.
Jon P.: I'll handle the customer communication draft; will post in #support after debrief.
incident-bot: Note: oncall pass to Lee scheduled at 2026-08-02T16:00:00Z. Please add handoff summary.
Alex: Handoff summary: mitigations applied (scale +2 nodes, fallback routing), customers notified, latency trending down, action items assigned above. I'll post a follow-up with more logs.
Lee (SRE): Thanks. I'll own the immediate follow-up and the autoscale audit. Leaving flag for runbook edits: add 'when to fallback to quantized models' section.
Sam T.: I'll file the observability ticket and add the alert thresholds.
Maria: I'll open the runbook PR and add the troubleshooting checklist + the commands Sam suggested.
Alex: Great work team. Marking this thread as the canonical debrief. We'll convert action items to issues and link them in the debrief doc.
Jon P.: Added a note to CS that a follow-up call is available to affected customers if they want.
Product Ops Bot: CS tickets created: CS-7123, CS-7124
Alex: Closing loop: last observed error rate back to normal at 2026-08-02T15:46:18Z. Will update last_message_ts after debrief complete.
Lee (SRE): ping if anything regresses; otherwise I'll update the runbook PR with the final wording.
